quickAnswer: Office cleaning in Fort Lauderdale, FL generally bills $36 to $62 per labor hour, a 1.04x index over national rates. A 5,000 sq ft carpeted office with two restrooms cleaned three times weekly costs about $476 to $803 per visit, or $6,185 to $10,444 per month; switch that same suite to ceramic tile and the range climbs to $6,879 to $11,600 per month.

blocks.text: Fort Lauderdale Rates at a Glance

Broward County janitorial labor is tighter than much of the Southeast. The janitor median wage reference near $17.16 per hour, plus Florida workers' compensation premiums and high-rise insurance requirements, gives Fort Lauderdale a 1.04x cost multiplier against national benchmarks. In practice that turns the national $0.09 to $0.15 per sq ft per visit band for 2,500 to 9,999 sq ft offices into roughly $0.094 to $0.156, and hourly billing for day porters, post-event cleanups, and hurricane-prep work runs $36 to $62 per hour.

The bigger cost driver here is not the index but the floor. South Florida offices lean heavily on ceramic and porcelain tile, which carries a 1.12x flooring factor because grout lines trap soil and need agitation, and because humidity keeps tile damp long enough to hold tracked-in sand. A Las Olas boutique suite with porcelain throughout will out-price a carpeted Cypress Creek office of the same size even before the tenant adds glass detailing.

blocks.text: These figures combine the national size-bracket rate, flooring and frequency multipliers, and $15 to $30 per restroom per visit, then apply the 1.04x index. Monthly totals use 4.33 weeks per month. Treat the low end as a lean scope from an owner-operated vendor and the high end as a fully supervised contract with dedicated quality inspections, which is what most high-rise property managers along Las Olas Boulevard and in the Downtown core require.

items: Las Olas: Street-level boutique offices and mid-rise towers with porcelain, glass storefronts, and heavy pedestrian sand. Budget nightly entry mopping and glass, even if interior suites are cleaned three nights a week.

Downtown and the New River towers: Class A high-rises with building-mandated vendor rosters, loading-dock check-in, and elevator reservations. Access friction adds labor time, which explains why bids cluster toward the upper half of the matrix.

Cypress Creek: Suburban office parks off I-95 with carpet-tile floor plates in the 10,000 to 24,999 sq ft bracket. This is where the most competitive Fort Lauderdale pricing appears, often $0.073 to $0.125 per sq ft per visit before adjustments.
Plantation: Medical office buildings and corporate campuses where patient restrooms and exam rooms raise restroom counts and require hospital-grade disinfectants with documented dwell times.

blocks.text: Salt Haze, Downpours, and Humidity: The Climate Line Items

Coastal salt haze leaves a film on exterior-facing glass that interior glass crews notice on sidelights and lobby doors, and tropical downpours turn every entrance into a wet-floor hazard by late afternoon. Humidity slows drying, so damp-mopped tile stays slick longer and grout stays dark. Ask vendors how they handle entry mats on rainy days, whether they use a dual-bucket system to keep dirty rinse water out of clean solution, and whether wet-floor signage stays posted until surfaces are dry.

Equipment matters for that last point. The Unger Commercial 15-Gallon Dual-Bucket SmartColor System separates clean solution from dirty rinse water in red and blue compartments, which prevents re-soiling grout lines with gray water. For quick sweeps before mopping a lobby, the Rubbermaid Commercial 36-Inch Cotton Dust Mop Frame & Handle covers wide corridors on a 360-degree swivel with a 60-inch handle. Day porters handling spills between visits can use the Rubbermaid Commercial HYGEN 18-Inch Microfiber Flat Mop Kit, whose onboard reservoir avoids dragging a bucket through occupied space.

blocks.title: Watch the hurricane-season scope gap
blocks.text: Most routine contracts exclude storm-prep and post-storm cleanup: moving electronics off floors, water extraction, and debris removal from vestibules. Negotiate a pre-agreed emergency hourly rate, typically at the upper end of the $36 to $62 band or the specialty band, so you are not paying surge pricing after a named storm.

blocks.title: High-rise insurance and bilingual crew coordination
blocks.text: South Florida building managers routinely require $1 million to $2 million general liability, umbrella coverage, workers' compensation, and additional-insured endorsements naming the owner and management company. Many crews are bilingual English and Spanish or Haitian Creole speakers, so request translated safety data sheets, OSHA HazCom training records, and a bilingual supervisor contact for after-hours issues.

faqs.q: Why is tile more expensive to clean than carpet in Fort Lauderdale?
faqs.a: Ceramic and porcelain tile need wet cleaning with grout agitation, and humidity keeps grout damp so it holds sand and soil. Pricing models apply roughly a 1.12x flooring factor to tile versus 1.0x for carpet, so a 5,000 sq ft three-night contract moves from about $6,185 to $6,879 per month at the low end.

faqs.q: What insurance should a Fort Lauderdale cleaning vendor carry?
faqs.a: Expect general liability of at least $1 million per occurrence, often $2 million aggregate, plus workers' compensation, commercial auto, umbrella coverage for high-rise buildings, and a fidelity bond. Your certificate of insurance should name your company and the building owner as additional insureds.

faqs.q: How are restroom disinfecting standards handled in medical offices in Plantation?
faqs.a: Crews should use EPA-registered disinfectants with the labeled dwell time observed, wear gloves, and be trained under the OSHA bloodborne pathogens standard. Ask the vendor for its exposure control plan, sharps-handling policy, and whether restrooms use color-coded cloths to avoid cross-contamination.

faqs.q: Can I save money by cleaning three nights instead of five?
faqs.a: Yes, but less than you might think. A 5,000 sq ft mixed-floor office runs about $10,250 to $17,309 per month at five nights; dropping to three nights cuts visits from 21.65 to 13.0 per month, yet per-visit cost rises about 5% because each visit recovers more soil. Many Las Olas tenants keep five-night restroom and trash service and move vacuuming to three nights.

faqs.q: Are green-certified products available from local vendors?
faqs.a: Most established Broward vendors can supply Green Seal or EPA Safer Choice cleaners and microfiber programs. Request product lists with safety data sheets so your HazCom file stays current, and confirm green products are still EPA-registered when used as disinfectants.
